slides.title: The 4 highest state minimum wages in 2027
slides.sub: Ranked by statewide hourly minimum wage on Jan. 1, 2027.

slides.heading: #1 Washington
body: Up 3.5% from $17.13. Washington raises it every year with inflation.
Workers aged 14 and 15 can be paid 85% of it: $15.07 an hour in 2027.

slides.heading: #2 Connecticut
body: Up 54 cents from $16.94. A 2019 state law ties the raise to a federal wage index, which rose 3.2%.

slides.heading: #3 California
body: California law adjusts the statewide minimum wage every year for inflation.
At 40 hours a week: $696 before taxes.

slides.heading: #4 Rhode Island
body: A 2025 state law raised it to $16 in 2026 and $17 in 2027.
At 40 hours a week: $680 before taxes.

slides.heading: Minimum wage in 2027
slides.note: Statewide hourly rate on Jan. 1, 2027. Texas uses the federal minimum wage.
slides.source: State labor offices; Texas Workforce Commission

slides.takeaway: Before your first job, look up your state's minimum wage. Then check your pay stub.

posts.caption:
Minimum wages go up in many states on Jan. 1, 2027. These are the four highest statewide rates:

1. Washington: $17.73 an hour (up 3.5%)
2. Connecticut: $17.48
3. California: $17.40
4. Rhode Island: $17.00

At 40 hours a week, Washington's rate works out to $709.20 before taxes. Texas still uses the federal minimum of $7.25, or $290 for 40 hours. Statewide rates only; some cities and regions set their own.

Data: Washington L&I (Sept. 30, 2026); Office of Gov. Lamont (Aug. 5, 2026); California DIR (Aug. 13, 2026); Office of Gov. McKee (Aug. 4, 2025); Texas Workforce Commission.
